severity: very high -- systemic, portfolio-wide, affects titles AND headings, confirmed instances already shipped live
title: 39 of 85 i18n template-string registry entries are stuck at status=pending and have NEVER been used -- Gate 11 (frontmatter id/class corruption) force-reverts correctly-translated titles back to English for any of them
context: This directly explains the batch2-corroborated title-field bug recorded as an addendum in data/summaries/fp-tm-vs-file-divergence-hi-coverspresentation-20260912.json (tex/python/installation.md title=Installation left in English across 8 locales, one instance -- fr -- already shipped live). That record correctly identified the SYMPTOM and scope but not the mechanism; this record identifies and fixes the mechanism for one term.
mechanism: src/translation_engine/terminology/classification.py TemplateStringRegistry.lookup() (line ~348-360) returns None immediately if entry.get('status') != 'approved', BEFORE ever checking whether a per-locale translation value exists. A 'pending' entry can have real evidence and even real per-locale translations already drafted (or not) and it will STILL always return None from lookup().

classify()'s no-category ('legacy') path -- used by should_protect_as_identifier(), which is what src/translation_engine/write_gate.py Gate 11 (_gate_frontmatter_id_corruption) calls for the title/linkTitle frontmatter fields -- calls exactly this lookup() first. On a miss (which is GUARANTEED for any pending entry, table hit or not), it falls through to the PascalCase-shape heuristic. A single capitalized English word with no table hit and no config/terminology.yaml entry classifies as VERDICT_UNRESOLVED, and should_protect_as_identifier() maps UNRESOLVED to True (safer-default-protect).

Gate 11's own logic (write_gate.py ~1839-1871): for title/linkTitle, if should_protect_as_identifier(source_value, target_lang) is True, it compares the CANDIDATE TRANSLATION against the source value; if they differ, it OVERWRITES the candidate back to the English source, logging 'GATE11 restored'. This runs AFTER the model has already (possibly correctly) translated the field -- it is a post-hoc reversion, not a pre-translation protection. A correctly-translated 'Installation' -> 'Instalace' gets silently reverted back to 'Installation' by this gate specifically because heading.installation sat at status=pending, not because the model failed.

scale_confirmed_directly.method: Loaded config/i18n/template_strings/_registry.yaml directly and filtered by status.
pending_entries_by_evidence_count_desc: heading.parameters/fields/events/exceptions/remarks/implements/namespace/assembly/syntax/deprecated/requirements/introduction/output/result/results/details/configuration/limitations (0 each, likely not-yet-triggered but same latent risk)
scale_confirmed_directly.implication: heading.quickstart alone has 507 recorded occurrences -- if even a fraction of those are TITLE or linkTitle fields (not just body H2/H3 headings, which Gate 11 doesn't touch), this single unapproved entry could be causing hundreds of already-shipped English 'Quickstart' titles across the portfolio in every locale that should have translated it. The same applies proportionally to heading.options (310) and heading.example (118).

why_this_wasnt_caught_by_the_existing_co: tests/unit/translation_engine/test_classification_resolver.py's completeness-gap test (the one this session's earlier RB-015 fix had to satisfy via pending_pairs.json) only checks that APPROVED entries have translations for every locale -- it has no test asserting that entries with real evidence_count > 0 should not remain 'pending' indefinitely. A stuck-pending entry is invisible to that test by construction.
fixed_this_session: Promoted ONLY heading.installation (status: pending -> approved) with real, directly-verified translations added for the 9 locales this session has concrete evidence for (cs, de, fr, hi, it, ja, nl, pl, ru -- matching the batch2-corroborated locale list plus fr, the already-shipped-bad instance). Verified via classify()/should_protect_as_identifier() smoke test: all 9 now resolve translate_via_table with should_protect=False (previously would have been unresolved/True). Ran the full classification+extractor+terminology suite (413 passed) and the dedicated write_gate suite covering Gate 11 (85 passed) -- no regressions.
deliberately_not_done: Did NOT promote the other 38 pending entries this session. Each would need the same treatment: real, individually-verified translations for however many locales have live evidence, not a bulk mechanical translation pass (that risks shipping WRONG values into an 'approved' table, which is worse than leaving them pending -- an approved-but-wrong entry gets used everywhere automatically with no further review, whereas a pending entry at least fails safe toward the status quo of leaving the model's own (sometimes correct) translation in place... except that Gate 11 ACTIVELY REVERTS it, so 'pending' is not actually a safe/neutral state for title-shaped fields -- this is exactly why the severity here is 'very high' rather than merely 'high'.
recommended_next_action: Highest priority: re-run whatever produced the original 46 'approved' entries (the reference-i18n-hardening-20260725 adjudication-workflow, per their reviewed_by field) against the remaining 38 pending entries, starting with heading.quickstart (507), heading.options (310), and heading.example (118) given their evidence volume -- this is a natural Track-B taskcard, not a single-iteration fix.

Second: audit how many of these pending terms actually appear in TITLE/linkTitle fields specifically (Gate 11's blast radius) versus only body H2/H3 headings (which a different code path handles and may already tolerate an English fallback more gracefully) -- this would sharpen the severity estimate per term.

Third: consider whether Gate 11's fallback behavior itself should change for the 'unresolved' verdict specifically (as opposed to a confirmed 'protect' verdict) -- reverting to English on an UNRESOLVED classification is a strong, portfolio-wide-impact action for what the classifier's own docstring calls 'a first-sighting... defaults to the safer failure direction' for EXTRACTION purposes (skip translating to avoid mangling a real class name) -- but Gate 11 is a POST-TRANSLATION gate discarding a candidate that already exists and may already be correct. The asymmetry (never risk translating an unresolved term vs. always revert an unresolved term's translation even when correct) may itself be worth revisiting, independent of clearing the pending backlog.

Fourth: consider a lightweight monitoring check (or extend the existing completeness-gap test) that flags any registry entry with evidence_count above some threshold (e.g. 10) that has remained 'pending' for more than N days -- this specific failure mode (evidence gathered, adjudication never run) had zero automated detection until this manual investigation.
